dedupe_keys.name: safecast citizen science radiation measurements worldwide cc0 dataset map and api

description: Safecast is a volunteer citizen science project that measures environmental radiation with its own open hardware devices and publishes the results openly. The site, read on 2026-09-26, reports about 5,000 deployed devices, 102 countries measured, 5,000 contributing volunteers and 66,000 daily measurements, a real-time map, an older map with data to August 2024, and Ukraine-specific maps. The data page offers a full CSV download of the Safecast data set, an API for querying and adding data, and uploads by registered users from bGeigie devices through the Safecast Drive apps. Data are published under a CC0 public domain designation, free for any use with attribution welcome; the website text is CC BY-NC 4.0, hardware designs are open and software is MIT unless stated. The licence page names the Momoko Ito Foundation as holder of the Safecast trademark. Caveats: measurements come from volunteers along their own routes, so coverage is uneven, and consumer devices are less precise than monitoring stations. Simulation uses are background radiation baselines around nuclear plants for hazard exposure and emergency response planning. Related records: data-iaea-news-ines-event-reports lists rated nuclear and radiological events.
